newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London rise with HSBC.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London rise with HSBC.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London were marked up in line with sharp gains in HSBC Holdings on Monday, after the banking giant's interim results surpassed expectations and prompted earnings upgrades.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index rose 162.88 points or one percent to 16,422.47 by 1405 GMT.
HSBC Holdings meanwhile, was trading at HK$272, up from HK$264 at the close in Hong Kong.
"Today's business has all been on the back of Hongkong Bank," said one dealer. "It reached a peak at HK$277 but then drifted back with the London market."

The bank reported pretax profit in sterling terms of 2.623 billion stg, up 13 percent from the previous year. Hang Seng Bank, a subsidiary of HSBC which reported ahead of the Hong Kong close saw profits rise 14.5 percent and was optimistic about the second half of the year.
Shares in Hang Seng were trading at HK$112.1 in London after a close of HK$111 in Hong Kong.
But dealers attributed most of the rise in the Reference Index to the gains in HongKong Bank.
In Hong Kong on Monday, investors had sold down the shares ahead of the results and a strong run up. The Hang Seng had fallen 119 points.

"Where we go tomorrow is anyone's guess," said the dealer. "People are getting concerned about Wall Street and think the market is in for a rocky couple of days...we might see some selling pressure at these sort of levels."
